resale_co.name: Certificate of Occupancy (Home Sale)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Allenhurst Code Official (Zoning / Code Officer)
resale_co.lead_time: The Borough code says a Certificate of Occupancy is granted or denied within ten days of the application.
requirements: Borough inspection of the home for compliance with all Borough ordinances
Applications for sales must include a current survey of the property
List all people who will occupy the home (each adult may need an affidavit as a member of a single family unit), school-age and pre-school children, and pets
Certificate of Smoke Alarm, Carbon Monoxide Alarm and Portable Fire Extinguisher Compliance (CSACMAPFEC) is required for all residential CO applications
All fees paid and all ordinances complied with before an inspection is scheduled

fees.label: Certificate of occupancy inspection and reinspection, houses (Borough code 9-3.3, Section 307.3)
Certificate of occupancy, houses (Borough application form)

resale_co.how_to_apply: Complete the Borough's Application for Certificate of Occupancy (check Sale), attach a current survey, sign under oath and pay the fee to the Borough of Allenhurst, 125 Corlies Avenue, Allenhurst, NJ 07711. The form says to call 732-413-8911 or email zoning@allenhurstnj.org to set up the inspection. Borough Hall: 732-531-2757.

evidence.quote: No owner, owner of rental properties, agent of owner, real estate agent or broker, firm, company, partnership, corporation or person or persons, shall sell, rent, transfer or occupy
evidence.doc_date: 2026-10-04 (Code 9-3.3, Section 307.1, read via ecode360 print view)

evidence.quote: Such a Certificate of Occupancy shall be granted or denied within ten days from the date of the application for same.
These fees shall become a dedicated fee to the Bureau of Fire Safety.
APPLICATIONS FOR SALES MUST INCLUDE A CURRENT SURVEY OF THE PROPERTY
An inspection will not be scheduled and a Certificate of Occupancy will not be issued unless the applicant has complied with all ordinances, including, but not limited to, payment of applicable fees.
This is required for all Residential CO Applications

resale_co.notes: Borough Code 9-3.3 adds Section 307 (Certificate of Occupancy) to the Borough's property maintenance code: no one may sell or transfer a dwelling without first getting a Certificate of Occupancy from the Code Official. The fee table is Commercial $150.00, Houses $125.00 and Apartments $100.00 per unit. The code text was read through the ecode360 print view. The home sale application (updated 6-27-2019) is a scanned PDF, so its quotes cannot be machine-checked; it lists the same fees and asks inspections to be set up at 732-413-8911 or zoning@allenhurstnj.org (the phone number is hard to read on the scan). The code officer's email (code@allenhurstnj.org) comes from the protected mailto link on the Zoning Board/Code Enforcement page. Construction permits for Allenhurst are handled by the City of Long Branch Building Department, and there is a construction moratorium from July 1 through Labor Day; neither is a resale step. Rental licenses and landlord registration are rental-only.

requirements: Smoke alarms on each level of the home, including basements (not attics or crawl spaces)
Smoke alarm and carbon monoxide alarm outside each separate sleeping area, within 10 feet of bedrooms
10-year sealed battery smoke alarms, unless the home has 110 volt alarms or a low voltage fire alarm system (low voltage systems need an annual certification)
Fire extinguisher rated 2A-10B:C, no more than 10 lbs, mounted within 10 feet of the kitchen in the path of egress, tagged or newly purchased with a receipt (form still lists it)

authorities.how_to_apply: Allenhurst is state-enforced for the fire code. Apply through the NJ DCA Division of Fire Safety (DCA service portal, 'Apply For Smoke Certification', choosing Monmouth County and Allenhurst) or call (609) 633-6132. The Borough's home sale CO packet also includes a smoke/CO certification application and says the certificate is required for every residential CO application.
authorities.contact_title: Fire Official (NJ Division of Fire Safety), per state directory

fire_cert.notes: The July 2026 LEA registry lists Allenhurst as state-enforced (S), and the state fire directory lists NJ Division of Fire Safety fire official Louis Kilmer, with Borough Hall (125 Corlies Ave, 732-531-2757) as the local smoke detector compliance contact. Current state fees under N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.9(d) are $45 / $90 / $161. Borough Code 9-3.3 still prints the older $35 / $70 / $125 smoke/CO fees 'dedicated to the Bureau of Fire Safety', and the Borough's smoke form is the old DCA paper form (2011), which says certificates are valid for six months; both are out of date. The Borough CO packet (2019) still requires a fire extinguisher; the state dropped it from the sale certificate in February 2025 (P.L.2025, c.19), so confirm.
